title: Liverpool’s Trent Kone-Doherty in talks over possible Molde transfer
content:
Liverpool winger Trent Kone-Doherty is in talks over a possible permanent move to Norwegian top-flight club Molde.

The Republic of Ireland under-21 international is out of contract at the end of the season and has been considering his options. The 19-year-old. who has made two senior Liverpool appearances, is keen to play more senior football as he approaches his 20th birthday in June.

Liverpool head coach Arne Slot gave him his first-team debut against Plymouth Argyle in the FA Cup last season, and he also featured in the Carabao Cup tie with Crystal Palace at Anfield last October.

However, most of his game time this season has been for Rob Page’s under-21s side in Premier 2. He has also been one of the standout performers in the club’s UEFA Youth League campaign – netting three goals in seven outings.

The transfer window in Norway is open until March 27, with Molde’s new league season getting underway against Rosenborg on March 14. A decision on Kone-Doherty’s future is expected in the next 24 hours.

Kone-Doherty arrived at Liverpool from his hometown club Derry City for a fee of £147,000 ($198,000) in the summer of 2022. Having initially shone for the under-18s, he signed his first professional contract in 2023 and subsequently made the step up to the under-21s.

In terms of the club’s talented young wingers, he’s found himself below both 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha and 19-year-old Kieran Morrison in the pecking order.

Ngumoha has made 15 senior appearances under Slot so far this season, while Morrison has only featured once but has been on the bench on four occasions over the past month.
